NUPath Attributes fetch-nupath.js

Updates the nuPath field for every course in all-courses.json by pulling from the official NUPath source. Tableau is the authoritative Registrar dashboard; the catalog HTML scrape is the fallback. After writing, patches are re-applied automatically.

Script
scripts/fetch-nupath.js
Output
public/northeastern/all-courses.json (nuPath fields updated)
Primary source
Tableau NUpath Attributes dashboard (tableau.northeastern.edu) — Registrar-maintained
Fallback source
catalog.northeastern.edu HTML scrape (parallel, 6 concurrent workers)

Two-source strategy

flowchart TD A["fetch-nupath.js --write"] --> B{"Tableau\navailable?"} B -->|Yes| C["Download Tableau CSV\n(tableau.northeastern.edu\n/Registrar/NUpathAttributes)"] B -->|No, or --catalog flag| D["Scrape catalog.northeastern.edu\nall subjects in parallel\n(6 workers, 300 ms delay)"] C --> E["Build nuPathMap: courseId → codes[]"] D --> E E --> F["Update nuPath for every course\nin all-courses.json"] F --> G["Write all-courses.json"] G --> H["Log nupath-auto-update entry\nto change-log.json"]

Why Tableau? The Registrar's Tableau dashboard is the same source the catalog ultimately derives NUPath designations from. When the catalog HTML is inconsistent or has parsing artifacts, Tableau is more reliable. When Tableau is behind a login or temporarily unavailable, the catalog scrape produces equivalent results.

Concurrency model (catalog fallback)

The catalog fallback scrapes all subject pages in parallel using a concurrency pool. Default: 6 concurrent workers, 300 ms delay between each worker's requests. Override with --concurrency 8 or NUPATH_DELAY_MS=150.

After a write — patches

This script updates all-courses.json directly, overwriting any previous nuPath values. Patches are not automatically re-applied by this script. After running fetch-nupath.js --write, run npm run data:nupath:apply:write to apply the nupath map to catalog-courses.json, then npm run data:patch:write to re-apply any manual corrections. The full flow:

node scripts/fetch-nupath.js --write        # update nuPath in all-courses.json
npm run data:nupath:apply:write             # apply nupath-map.json → catalog-courses.json
npm run data:patch:write                    # re-apply manual patches on top

When run via the Trigger tab's ⚡ Run locally button, the server runs the script as configured in catalog-check-server.js — check the ADAPTER_DEFS there to see exactly which flags are passed.

When triggered by GitHub Actions, triggeredBy is the actor username and runId is the Actions run ID (links to the run from the Log tab).

Usage

node scripts/fetch-nupath.js               # dry run — shows diff
node scripts/fetch-nupath.js --write        # write all-courses.json
node scripts/fetch-nupath.js --catalog      # force catalog strategy (skip Tableau)
node scripts/fetch-nupath.js --tableau      # force Tableau strategy (error if unavailable)
node scripts/fetch-nupath.js --concurrency 8  # more parallel workers (catalog mode)
